Detection does not establish a general correction procedure. The paper includes useful ablations of initialization, annealing, proposal strategies, and corruption location. Appendix C.6 also provides quantitative evidence supporting the proxy reward on short PRONTOQA chains.

AVI demonstrates transfer across nearby reasoning lengths and preliminary downstream benefits. The authors acknowledge the limitations of synthetic corruption and include experiments on naturally generated reasoning.
weaknesses: The main evaluation has limited validity for realistic error detection. GSM8K and COMMONSENSEQA reference chains generated by GPT-4.1 are assumed entirely correct without an independent annotation audit. Artificial negations and numerical perturbations differ substantially from natural reasoning failures; examples even contain explicit cues such as 'False:' and 'Incorrect:'. These artifacts could support strong performance without robust reasoning verification.

Practical evidence is considerably weaker than the headline results. VS requires the correct answer, so deployment claims depend on AVI. On natural chains, PRONTOQA accuracy improves from 0.712 to 0.730, while COMMONSENSEQA improves from 0.749 with standard Self-Refine to 0.756 with AVI. There is no corresponding natural-error evaluation on GSM8K, and within-domain fine-tuning plus nearby-length transfer does not establish broad zero-shot generalization.

The comparisons do not sufficiently isolate the contribution. Beyond prompting and search baselines, the paper needs comparisons with learned verifiers or automatic process-supervision methods under comparable supervision. AVI should also be compared with identical fine-tuning using directly prompted pseudo-labels. Critically, there is no ablation separating the label prior P(v|x,z) from the answer-likelihood term P(y*|x,z,v), leaving the benefit of the proposed joint reward unresolved.

Some probabilistic interpretations exceed what is established. In Section 2.2, evaluating a truncated prompt does not cause an autoregressive LM to marginalize omitted veracity variables under the original model. Annealed search and supervised distillation also do not establish sampling from the original posterior. These can be useful heuristics, but their distinction from posterior inference needs clearer treatment.

Reproducibility is weakened by concrete omissions and inconsistencies. The mathematical reward template in Appendix A.3 omits the candidate veracity vector, and the actual five demonstrations are not supplied. Search temperature endpoints differ between Section 4.3 and Appendix A.3 without clarification. The Qwen-4B COMMONSENSEQA single-bit result is 0.935 in Table 1 but 0.860 in Table 7, with no explanation of the changed setting.

The efficiency and scalability claims remain narrow. Length scaling reaches only five hops, approximately 13 statements, and timing is reported for one model on PRONTOQA. A nominal single VS sample already involves greedy initialization with multiple likelihood evaluations. Clear accounting of those evaluations and pseudo-label generation costs is needed to substantiate the broader efficiency claim.

Table 7 reports COMMONSENSEQA single-bit performance of 0.860 for Qwen3-4B, versus 0.935 in Table 1, without explaining the difference.

The generalization and scalability claims exceed the demonstrated scope. Length experiments reach only five hops, approximately 13 statements. AVI uses thousands of task-specific training examples, and its inference template still contains few-shot demonstrations; describing this broadly as zero-shot generalization to novel contexts is misleading. Transfer across substantially different tasks, error types, or longer reasoning traces is not established.
